body:
Good morning, Kern County. It’s a comfortable, dry Friday with a high near 83 degrees and a mild overnight low around 61, and the air quality sits at a moderate 68. Our top story touches thousands of local families: a new federal public charge rule could change the green card path for many Kern County immigrants, and we’ll break down what that means this morning.

## The Kern Overnight

Overnight, Bakersfield’s quietest hours still had their share of activity. Shortly before 1 a.m., an officer broadcast a Code 33, clearing the radio channel for emergency traffic, as units pursued a vehicle that appeared to be yielding westbound on Hampton Avenue. The vehicle eventually stopped at a different block than first reported, with multiple units converging before the channel was cleared back to normal. No injuries were reported, but it was the kind of coordinated response that keeps the overnight dispatch sharp.

A little after 2:20 a.m., officers and Liberty Ambulance paramedics were sent to a park on Hawthorne Avenue after a man with facial injuries said he had been jumped. Dispatch described him as wearing a black shirt and blue jeans, last seen walking eastbound on Hawthorne. Fire crews were also cleared to an updated address on the same street a few minutes later, though the situation appeared to settle. Earlier in the evening, Battalion 6 responded to a refuse fire burning inside a decommissioned tank on a property that crews recognized from previous calls involving burning copper wire. The assignment was downgraded, and companies already on scene handled the fire.

Elsewhere, officers were sent to an apartment in the 6200 block of Victor Street after a caller reported a man and a woman removing boards from the place and entering. And at a car wash in the 8100 block of East Brundage Lane, a prowler report came in with descriptions of a woman in a tie-dye shirt and black shorts and a man in a hunter-green ball cap, green shirt, and blue jeans — dispatch noted the pair might be connected to an earlier vandalism report. The rest of the night’s log included a welfare check on Smith Street, a disturbance on Breezeway Drive involving an ex-boyfriend who wouldn’t leave, a reported battery east of Haley Street and Panorama Drive, and a semi parked on the right-hand shoulder of a highway.

## Today's weather

Expect a mostly sunny Friday with a high near 83 degrees and a low around 61 tonight. As of this morning, thermometers at Meadows Field show 61 degrees, so it’s a crisp start. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is 68, which falls in the moderate range — sensitive individuals may want to take it easy outdoors. No active fires are currently listed for the county.

## Top stories

**According to 23ABC, thousands of Kern County immigrants could lose their path to a green card under a new Trump administration rule expanding the definition of "public charge."** The rule allows immigration officials to review an applicant's past use of government assistance, including benefits like Medicare, which roughly half of Kern County relies on. Local immigration attorney Win Eaton said the standard asks whether an applicant is likely to depend on government aid in the future, and he stressed that immigrants are essential to running the country. California Attorney General Rob Bonta pushed back, saying no family should have to choose between healthcare and a legal future.

**KGET 17 reports that a scratch-off ticket worth $2 million was sold in Shafter.** The winning ticket was purchased in the small Kern County city east of Bakersfield, though no further details about the store or winner were immediately available. It’s a nice reminder that luck can strike close to home.

**23ABC reports that advocates and survivors are working to change how Kern County spots human trafficking, saying the warning signs often hide in plain sight.** At a “Fall Into Awareness” training held Sept. 17 at CityServe, the Kern Coalition Against Human Trafficking taught local professionals to recognize red flags like unexpected gifts, school absences, troubling online activity, and specific symbols. Survivor Ofelia Flores said she didn’t realize what was happening to her because she didn’t know she had a voice. Dr. Angela Look, a coalition steering member, noted that less than 1% of trafficking cases involve kidnapping — making it far easier to miss victims who appear to live normal lives.

**KGET 17 reports that Bakersfield police are reopening a vexing cold case from 1923 involving a murdered woman and a toddler described as "robust."** The case has puzzled investigators for more than a century, and the department is taking a fresh look with modern eyes. It’s a reminder that some mysteries never fully leave the community’s memory.

**Bakersfield Now reports that a Fresno man was convicted of attempting to meet a decoy he believed was a 15-year-old boy for sex.** The conviction follows an undercover operation, though the news outlet did not provide additional details in its headline. The case underscores the ongoing work of local law enforcement to protect minors online.

## Something good

Here’s one to brighten your morning: Adventist Health will host free breast screening appointments for uninsured residents across Kern County, opening the door to important preventive care for families who might otherwise go without. It’s a small gesture with huge meaning — giving local women a reassuring opportunity to catch health problems early.

## Coming up this week

Plenty of ways to get involved this week. On Monday, Sept. 21, the Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee meets at noon, followed Tuesday, Sept. 22, by the Homelessness Committee at the same time. Friday, Sept. 25, the Laws and Legislation Committee convenes at noon. All are public meetings, and residents are welcome to attend.

For a night out, the Fox Theater has you covered. Tonight, Friday, Sept. 18, brings “It’s A 2000s Party: Bakersfield” — a throwback dance night for anyone who misses the era of flip phones and ringtones. Monday, Sept. 21, the Fox’s Cults & Classics series screens “What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?” — a deliciously creepy film perfect for the season. The indie rock band Men I Trust plays Wednesday, Sept. 23, with special guest Evan Wright, and comedian Mike Sherm takes the stage Saturday, Sept. 26. Looking further ahead, the Cults & Classics series continues Oct. 5 with Mel Brooks’ “Young Frankenstein.” Whether you’re testifying at a committee meeting or laughing through a cult classic, there’s a little something for everyone in Kern County this week.
